body.statement: Can \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{face}}\) be used to construct a computable random set whose support functions contract at the \(\sqrt n\) rate and whose coverage of \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) remains uniform along sequences approaching intersections of optimal faces, without imposing a unique optimizer or selecting one population face?
body.justification: This is the unresolved bridge between conservative exact coverage and informative local inference at nonsmooth policy ties.
body.gap: FangSantos2019DirectionalInference handles directionally differentiable maps, while LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence treats fixed-matrix LP sets; neither establishes uniform \(\sqrt n\)-rate contraction for the moving-coefficient categorical-instrument optimizer graph.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether tie-heavy categorical-treatment applications can receive informative rather than merely valid optimizer sets.
